arabic: تَجَاهَلَ الْمُشْرِفُ اعْتِرَاضَ الطَّالِبِ عَلَى تَحْدِيدِ مَكَانِ الاِمْتِحَانِ، وَلَمْ يَرْضَ الطَّالِبُ.

gpt_reason: A coherent sentence with correct grammar and an accurate translation.
sonnet_reason: Grammatical and plausible scenario; translation accurate.

arabic: لَمْ يَتَجَاهَلِ الطَّالِبُ شُحُوبَ جَارِهِ، فَحَمَلَهُ إِلَى عِيَادَةٍ لِرِعَايَتِهِ.

gpt_reason: A plausible response to a neighbor appearing unwell; grammar and translation are correct.

arabic: تَوَقَّعْتُ لُغْزًا فِي هَذِهِ الْأُسْطُورَةِ، لَكِنَّ سُطُورَهَا لَغْوٌ بِلَا تَشْوِيقٍ.

arabic: هَاتِ يَا اِبْنِي نِصْفَ الزُّبْدَةِ وَرُبْعَ وِعَاءِ الخَرْدَلِ مِنَ الخِزَانَةِ.
english: Son, bring me half the butter and a quarter of the mustard jar from the cupboard.
gpt_reason: A plausible household request; the quarter-jar quantity is understood as referring to its contents in both languages.
sonnet_reason: Asking for 'half the butter and a quarter of the mustard jar' is odd; 'هات' with 'يا ابني' fine, but quantity of a jar is contrived and missing 'لي'. Reads as forced word-list.

arabic: شِرَاءُ التَّنُّورَةِ مُتْعِبٌ، فَالمَقَاسُ خَاطِئٌ وَالحَجْمُ صَغِيرٌ جِدًّا.

gpt_reason: The sizing complaint is coherent despite some redundancy. The translation preserves its meaning.
sonnet_reason: 'المقاس خاطئ والحجم صغير' is redundant; translation 'fit is too small' conflates size/fit. Also 'buying is tiring' is contrived.

arabic: أَضَافَ الطَّالِبُ حَفْنَةً مِنَ السُّكَّرِ إِلَى خَلِيطِ الزُّبْدَةِ وَالزَّيْتِ.
english: The student added a handful of sugar to the butter and oil mixture.
gpt_reason: Grammatical, plausible cooking scene; the translation is accurate.
sonnet_reason: Simple, coherent cooking sentence; translation accurate.

arabic: نَاوَلَتْنِي الجَارَةُ حَفْنَةً مِنَ القَمْحِ وَخَلِيطًا مِنَ الزُّبْدَةِ وَالسُّكَّرِ.

gpt_reason: A plausible exchange of cooking ingredients; the translation is accurate.

arabic: الطَّحَّانُ الصَّبُورُ كَنَسَ الْمَطْحَنَةَ، ثُمَّ أَغْلَقَ الْبَوَّابَةَ فِي ذَلِكَ الْيَوْمِ.

gpt_reason: Grammatical, plausible, and accurately translated.
sonnet_reason: Coherent narrative sentence; grammatical and accurate.

arabic: رَمَّ النَّجَّارُ فِي الجَرَاجِ مُؤَخَّرَةَ العَرَبَةِ وَعَجَلَتَهَا بِقَضِيبٍ خَاصٍّ.
english: In the garage, the carpenter repaired the rear of the cart and its wheel with a special rod.
gpt_reason: Plausible repair of a wooden cart. رَمَّ means 'repaired': [Arabic Language Academy](https://www.arabicacademy.gov.eg/ar/محرك-البحث/معجم/dic-19/رم).
sonnet_reason: Carpenter repairing cart with 'a rod' is awkward; 'رم' and 'الجراج' plus 'قضيب خاص' are contrived and the sentence is forced.

arabic: الْمَنْسَفُ أَكْلِي الْمُفَضَّلُ، لَكِنَّ الصَّيَّادِيَةَ عِنْدَ هَذَا الطَّبَّاخِ الْبَارِعِ تُضَاهِيهِ.
english: Mansaf is my favorite food, but this skillful cook’s sayadieh rivals it.
gpt_reason: A natural comparison between two dishes; the English preserves the meaning.
sonnet_reason: Plausible comparison of mansaf and sayadieh (a fish dish); grammatical. Translation accurate.

arabic: نَمَّ بَعْضُ الأَصْدِقَاءِ عَلَى العَزْبَاءِ، لَكِنَّهَا دَافَعَتْ عَنِ اسْتِغْنَائِهَا عَنِ الرَّجُلِ بِعِنَادٍ.
english: Some friends gossiped about the single woman, but she stubbornly defended her not needing a man.
gpt_reason: Somewhat formal but plausible. The English conveys the gossip and her insistence on independence.
sonnet_reason: Grammatical and plausible; 'نم على' means gossip/inform on, acceptable. Translation fine.

arabic: فِي الصَّبَاحِ، أَيْقَظَتِ الأَمِيرَةُ جَوَادَهَا بِقُبْلَةٍ، وَدَاعَبَتْهُ، ثُمَّ هَمَسَتْ: أَهْلًا.

gpt_reason: Plausible affectionate interaction with a horse, especially in a story; accurately translated.
sonnet_reason: Charming, plausible story sentence; grammatical and accurate.

arabic: عَجِبَ الْوَلَدُ بُرْهَةً مِنْ ضِيَاءِ الْهِلَالِ الَّذِي لَمْ يَأْفُلْ.
english: For a moment, the boy marveled at the glow of the crescent that had not yet set.
gpt_reason: Slightly literary but plausible and grammatical; 'had not yet set' fits the Arabic context.
sonnet_reason: Grammatical, literary but plausible. عجب من is fine; يأفل (set) used correctly for the crescent.

arabic: تَسَلَّقَ السِّنْجَابُ العِمَارَةَ فِي بُرْهَةٍ، فَدَهِشَ الوَلَدُ وَالرَّجُلُ أَيْضًا.
english: The squirrel climbed the building in a moment, and the boy and the man were both astonished.
gpt_reason: Grammatical and plausible; the translation accurately conveys the event and reactions.
sonnet_reason: A squirrel climbing a building 'in a moment' is odd but plausible; however 'بُرْهَة' means a span of time, not an instant, and 'فِي بُرْهَةٍ' is awkward. Also 'دَهِشَ الوَلَدُ وَالرَّجُلُ' is okay, but the overall phrasing is unnatural.

arabic: المَنْسَفُ أَكْلِي المُفَضَّلُ، وَأَنَا مُولَعٌ جِدّاً بِالبَهَارِ وَالنَّعْنَاعِ.

gpt_reason: A coherent statement of food preferences with an accurate translation.
sonnet_reason: Natural, grammatical. Mansaf as favorite food and fondness for spices and mint is plausible.

arabic: تَذَمَّرَ الطِّفْلُ الآنَ لِأَنَّ فِي حَنْجَرَتِهِ خَدَرًا وَلُعَابُهُ مَالِحٌ.
english: The child is complaining now because there is numbness in his throat and his saliva is salty.
gpt_reason: A plausible description of a child's symptoms. With الآن, the translation reasonably conveys the immediate complaint.
sonnet_reason: Forced combination of symptoms (numb throat, salty saliva) with 'now' and a child complaining; reads like a word-list sentence and is implausible phrasing.

arabic: دَعَمَ الْوَزِيرُ إِيقَافَ حَبْسِ الْفَقِيرِ الْبَائِسِ لِأَنَّ حَالَتَهُ مُؤْلِمَةٌ.

arabic: شَاهَدْنَا فِلْمًا مُضْحِكًا جِدًّا، فَتَحَوَّلَ مِزَاجُ بَابَا المُرْهَقِ إِلَى سُرُورٍ.

arabic: رَغِبَ الجَارُ اللَّهِمُ فِي كُلِّ طَعَامِ المَأْدُبَةِ: الرُّزِّ المَنْدِي وَالفُلْفُلِ المَحْشِيِّ.

arabic: النَّمِرُ قَفَزَ عَلَى الْحَارِسِ بِضَرَاوَةٍ، لَكِنَّ الْحَارِسَ نَجَا بِحِيلَةٍ.
